question.prompt: An integer \(N\) is selected at random in the range \(1\leq N \leq 2020\) . What is the probability that the remainder when \(N^{16}\) is divided by \(5\) is \(1?\)

solutions.title: Track the units digit
solutions.explanation:
The units digit of \(N\) determines the units digit of every power of \(N\). A number has remainder \(1\) when divided by \(5\) exactly when its units digit is \(1\) or \(6\).

To reach the sixteenth power, square four times. The table records only the units digit at each stage; each new entry comes from squaring the preceding entry and keeping its units digit.
\[
\begin{array}{c|cccc}
\text{Units digit of }N & N^2 & N^4 & N^8 & N^{16}\\
\hline
0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\\
1,9 & 1 & 1 & 1 & 1\\
2,8 & 4 & 6 & 6 & 6\\
3,7 & 9 & 1 & 1 & 1\\
4,6 & 6 & 6 & 6 & 6\\
5 & 5 & 5 & 5 & 5
\end{array}
\]
Thus all starting units digits except \(0\) and \(5\) work, giving eight successful digits.

Since \(2020=202\cdot10\), each units digit occurs exactly \(202\) times from \(1\) through \(2020\). The probability is therefore
\[
\frac{8\cdot202}{10\cdot202}=\frac45.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{\frac45}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
